summary: Edge ingress annotation sideloading strips tenant claim, causing RBAC role lookup to fail and 403s
description: Issue summary: Customer reports sudden authorization failures (403) for all API calls from their private VPC deployment after a platform edge upgrade. Impact: API requests authenticated successfully at the IdP level but Redwood returns 403 due to missing tenant-scoped role lookup. Environment: private VPC deployment, prod-us-east, ingress-proxy v1.4.1 -> recently upgraded to 1.4.2 in customer cluster. Symptoms: Intermittent and then persistent 403s for existing tokens; session cookies and id_tokens appear valid. Hypothesis: Ingress annotation "sideload-claims" introduced in 1.4.2 is stripping or renaming the tenant_id claim header before requests reach the auth service, causing RBAC to fail to find tenant-bound role bindings.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private VPC with ingress-proxy v1.4.2 and enable edge-annotations: sideload-claims=true
2) Obtain a valid OIDC id_token for user scoped to tenant 'nimbus-123'
3) Send a standard Generate/Chat request via customer's ingress endpoint with Authorization: Bearer <id_token>
4) Observe 403 responses from Redwood API; check auth service audit log for 'role lookup: missing tenant claim' entries
logs: ingress-proxy[2026-03-10T09:24:15Z] INFO: received request /v1/generate headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted> x-claims-sideload: true
auth-service[2026-03-10T09:24:15Z] WARN: role-lookup: tenant_id header missing; token_sub=jane.doe@nimbus.com subject_sub=jane.doe@nimbus.com
rbac-sync[2026-03-10T09:24:15Z] ERROR: no role bindings found for subject=jane.doe@nimbus.com tenant=<empty> returning 403
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Confirmed tokens validated by introspection; IdP reports correct tenant claim in token payload
Replayed traffic through staging ingress-proxy v1.4.1: tenant claim preserved and RBAC lookup succeeds
Replayed same token through ingress-proxy v1.4.2: header 'x-tenant-id' absent when request forwarded internally
Hypothesis strengthened: new sideload behavior in 1.4.2 moves claims into a JSON envelope but also drops legacy x-tenant-id header unless 'preserve-legacy-headers=true' set
Temporary mitigation tested: setting ingress annotation 'sideload-claims-preserve: true' preserves x-tenant-id and restores traffic for a subset of requests
Root cause likely: change in default annotation behavior in 1.4.2; private customer clusters with older RBAC service expected legacy header name
comments: Support (Aisha): Reached out to customer at 2026-03-10 09:40Z to gather logs and confirm cluster upgrade timing.
Customer (N. Patel - Nimbus SRE): Cluster was auto-upgraded to ingress-proxy 1.4.2 on 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC. We didn't change RBAC config. All requests broke after upgrade.
Eng (Liam): Reproduced in our staging: ingress-proxy 1.4.2 by default removes legacy x-tenant-id header. Created a test ingress with sideload-claims-preserve=true and validated role lookup succeeds.
Eng (Liam): Created PR to ingress-proxy to add a rollout flag and default to preserve legacy headers for private deployments (see related PR). Requesting backport and hotfix release.
Support (Aisha): Applied customer workaround annotation and validated customer reported restored traffic within 10 minutes. Working with customer to schedule controlled rollout of hotfix.
Customer (N. Patel): Appreciated quick workaround; requested written postmortem and timeline for controlled fix across other private clusters.
resolution: Workaround applied: added ingress annotation 'sideload-claims-preserve=true' to restore x-tenant-id header and immediate traffic. Engineering produced hotfix PR to default preserve-legacy-headers for private VPCs and backport to ingress-proxy v1.4.3. Follow-up: schedule channel deployment of v1.4.3, add regression test in CI verifying tenant header preservation, and update changelog/runbook to call out annotation behavior change.
next_steps: 1) Backport hotfix and cut ingress-proxy v1.4.3 (eng)
2) Coordinate maintenance window with Nimbus to roll v1.4.3 to their clusters (CS + SRE)
3) Add CI test covering sideloaded claim preservation for private deployments (QA/Eng)
4) Publish postmortem and update Confluence runbook on ingress annotations (Support)
5) Review auto-upgrade rollout policy for private clusters to avoid silent incompatible changes (PM/Infra)
